intelligence.essence: Every click takes you one level deeper — never sideways. Click the orb, get its stats. Click a stat, get its time breakdown in bars. Every click must show something. Nothing dead, nothing decorative.
intelligence.human_view:
Shawn was testing the drill-downs and saw the confusion: chart-switcher buttons that changed the view, but no way to go deeper. He redesigned the hierarchy live: the orb opens the section's stats (the four sub-stats), and clicking any stat inside opens that stat's time breakdown — day by day, hour by hour — in bars. Not the chart buttons. The stats themselves are the doors.

"You're going to click the orb for the section then it goes in and gives you the stats... but then if you click the stat that's displayed that stat will get displayed in bars... you click the button you go into the inner stats they give you those four stats then you click any of those stats then you get the bar stats."
intelligence.simple_view: It's like opening drawers inside drawers. Tap a round orb and you see its four helper numbers. Tap one of those numbers and you see it drawn as bars, day by day and hour by hour. Every tap shows you something new — nothing is just for decoration.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, it's like a dresser: you open one drawer and find four tidy compartments, and each compartment opens to show you the whole story, day by day. Every drawer you open has something real in it — no empty drawers, no fake handles.
intelligence.naya_view: I build navigation as depth, never sideways drift: orb → its sub-stats → the stat's time breakdown in bars. The stats themselves are the doors; chart-switcher buttons change a view, they never substitute for depth. Any control that shows nothing on click is a lie and gets removed.
intelligence.ai_view: This is the answer to "what's the story?" — the third question of the Smart Stats bullseye. A dashboard that only shows totals is a poster. The drill-down is what makes it an instrument: where am I (gauge), what's driving it (orbs), what's the story (drill down). And the law inside it — every click must show something — is the anti-dead-control rule: a control that does nothing is a lie.
